lessonTitle: Lumbar Puncture: Landmarks, Layers and Why Below the Cord

blocks.text: A 20-year-old student has a headache, fever and a stiff neck. To confirm meningitis the team needs cerebrospinal fluid, and the safest place to get it lies at the bottom of the back, well below the point where the spinal cord ends. Where exactly to put the needle, and why there, is a question of surface anatomy and development.

blocks.markdown: The spinal cord is shorter than the vertebral canal. In the early fetus the cord fills the canal, but the vertebral column grows faster than the cord, so the cord appears to "ascend". In the adult the cord ends as the **conus medullaris** at about the level of L1 to L2. In the newborn it ends lower, at about L3. Below the conus, the lumbar and sacral nerve roots descend in the subarachnoid space as the **cauda equina**, bathed in CSF.

blocks.title: Lumbar cistern
blocks.text: The expanded subarachnoid space below the conus medullaris. It contains CSF, the cauda equina and the filum terminale, and ends at the lower border of the dural sac at about S2.

rows: End of dural sac and subarachnoid space
Extends below the conus, as in the adult
Puncture at L3-L4 or L4-L5 is below the cord
Choose a lower interspace so the cord is not reached
blocks.caption: Level of the cord and subarachnoid space with age.

blocks.markdown: A needle placed in the lumbar cistern meets nerve roots that are free in the CSF. The roots float and tend to be pushed aside by the needle, whereas the cord is tethered and fixed and can be damaged. This is why a lumbar puncture is done below the conus medullaris and not higher in the spine.

**Surface landmarks.** The line joining the highest points of the iliac crests (the **supracristal plane**, also called Tuffier's line) crosses the L4 spinous process or the L4-L5 interspace in most adults. The L3-L4 interspace is therefore found just above this line. The spinous processes in the midline are palpated between and the patient is positioned lying on the side with knees drawn up, or sitting and leaning forward, to flex the lumbar spine and open the gaps between the laminae.

blocks.title: Locating the interspace
blocks.prompt: A resident places her fingers on the iliac crests and runs a line between the highest points. She finds the spinous process where the line crosses the midline. Which interspace is selected for an L3-L4 puncture and why?

steps.text: The supracristal plane crosses the spine at L4 (or the L4-L5 gap).
The L3-L4 interspace lies one level above, so move up by one spinous process from the point where the line crosses.
Another interspace is L4-L5, immediately below the plane, which is also below the end of the cord.
Both are safe in an adult because the cord ends at about L1 to L2, well above these levels.

blocks.answer: L3-L4 lies just above the supracristal plane; L4-L5 lies just below. Both are below the adult conus.

blocks.markdown: **Layers traversed** by a midline needle, from superficial to deep: skin; subcutaneous fat (superficial fascia); **supraspinous ligament** (over the tips of the spinous processes); **interspinous ligament**; **ligamentum flavum** (between adjacent laminae, a tough elastic ligament); the **epidural space** containing fat and the internal vertebral venous plexus; **dura mater**; **arachnoid mater**; then the **subarachnoid space** with CSF. Many operators feel a "pop" as the needle passes the ligamentum flavum and again through the dura.

blocks.title: Tracing the needle
blocks.prompt: A needle is advanced in the midline of the L4-L5 interspace. Describe the layers crossed and where the feeling of resistance changes.

steps.text: The needle passes skin and subcutaneous fat, which offer little resistance.
It crosses the supraspinous and then the interspinous ligaments, giving a firm resistance.
The ligamentum flavum is the toughest layer, with marked resistance, and the needle emerges into the loose epidural space where resistance falls.
Further advance pierces the dura and arachnoid, often with a second pop, and CSF flows at the hub.

blocks.answer: Skin, fat, supraspinous and interspinous ligaments, ligamentum flavum, epidural space, dura, arachnoid, CSF.

blocks.title: Why below the cord
blocks.text: The cord stops at L1 to L2, but the CSF-filled sac continues to S2. A needle in the lumbar cistern meets mobile roots rather than the cord.

blocks.title: Cautions
blocks.text: Raised intracranial pressure can make a lumbar puncture dangerous because withdrawal of CSF may allow downward herniation; clinicians assess for this before puncture, for example by checking for focal signs or imaging when indicated. Bleeding disorders and local infection are other contraindications. Post-puncture headache may follow leakage of CSF through the dural hole.

points: The adult cord ends at L1 to L2 (L3 in the newborn) and the subarachnoid space continues to about S2, forming the lumbar cistern with the cauda equina.
The supracristal plane crosses L4 or the L4-L5 interspace, so L3-L4 lies just above it.
Layers: skin, fat, supraspinous ligament, interspinous ligament, ligamentum flavum, epidural space, dura, arachnoid, subarachnoid space.

questions.stem: A line joining the highest points of the iliac crests is drawn on an adult's back. At which vertebral level does it most commonly cross the midline?

options.text: L4 spinous process or L4-L5 interspace

questions.correctOptionText: L4 spinous process or L4-L5 interspace

distractorRationale.a: Correct: the supracristal plane crosses at about L4.
distractorRationale.c: S2 is the end of the dural sac, not the crest line.
distractorRationale.d: L1-L2 marks the conus, not the crest line.

questions.explanation: The supracristal plane crosses the spine at L4 or L4-L5 in most adults. L3-L4 lies just above it.

questions.stem: A doctor wants to puncture one level above the supracristal plane. Which interspace is this?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: one interspace above L4-L5 is L3-L4.
distractorRationale.c: L1-L2 is the level of the conus medullaris.

questions.explanation: If the plane crosses L4, the interspace immediately above is L3-L4. Starting here keeps the needle well below the adult cord.

questions.stem: Which ligament is most superficial of those crossed by a midline needle?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: the supraspinous ligament lies over the tips of the spinous processes.
distractorRationale.b: The interspinous ligament lies deeper between the spinous processes.
distractorRationale.c: The ligamentum flavum is deeper still, between the laminae.
distractorRationale.d: The posterior longitudinal ligament lies inside the canal behind the vertebral bodies and is not crossed.

questions.explanation: A midline needle crosses supraspinous, interspinous and then ligamentum flavum. The posterior longitudinal ligament lies anterior to the dura and is not reached.

questions.stem: Immediately after passing through the ligamentum flavum, the needle enters which space?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: the epidural space lies between the ligamentum flavum and the dura.
distractorRationale.b: The subarachnoid space lies deep to the dura and arachnoid.
distractorRationale.c: The subdural space is only a potential space.
distractorRationale.d: The disc lies in front of the canal and is not on the needle's path.

questions.explanation: Deep to the ligamentum flavum is the epidural space containing fat and veins. The next layers are dura mater and arachnoid, then CSF.

questions.stem: In an adult, the spinal cord ends at about L1 to L2, whereas the subarachnoid space continues down to about S2.
questions.explanation: The conus medullaris lies at L1 to L2 but the dural sac extends to about S2. This difference creates the lumbar cistern, which can be sampled safely.

questions.stem: In a 3-week-old infant, why is an interspace lower than the one chosen in older children traditionally preferred?

options.text: The spinal cord ends lower, at about L3, in the newborn
The vertebral column is longer than the cord
The dural sac ends at L1

questions.correctOptionText: The spinal cord ends lower, at about L3, in the newborn

distractorRationale.a: Correct: the newborn cord ends lower, about L3.
distractorRationale.b: The cord is shorter than the column in all ages.
distractorRationale.c: The dural sac ends lower, not at L1.
distractorRationale.d: The cauda equina is present at all ages.

questions.explanation: In the newborn, the cord extends lower than in the adult, so the conus may be at about L3. A lower interspace therefore keeps the needle in the cistern.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man's lumbar puncture is performed with him curled on his side with knees drawn up. What is the anatomical purpose of this position?

options.text: Flexion opens the gaps between the laminae and spinous processes
It moves the conus medullaris down

questions.correctOptionText: Flexion opens the gaps between the laminae and spinous processes

distractorRationale.a: Correct: flexion widens the interspinous and interlaminar spaces.
distractorRationale.b: Position does not move the cord down to any useful extent.
distractorRationale.c: The roots are not lengthened by positioning in a way that guides the needle.
distractorRationale.d: The sac is not shortened by posture.

questions.explanation: Lumbar flexion separates the spinous processes and laminae so the needle can pass between them. It does not change the end of the cord.

questions.stem: List the layers a lumbar puncture needle passes through in the midline, from skin to CSF.
markingGuide: Dura mater and arachnoid mater, then subarachnoid space.
questions.explanation: Each layer has a recognisable resistance, with the ligamentum flavum being the toughest. The final two membranes are crossed together to reach CSF.

questions.stem: Explain why lumbar puncture is performed below the termination of the cord, and why the level differs between neonates and adults.
markingGuide: Cord ends at L1 to L2 in adults.
Subarachnoid space continues to about S2, containing the cauda equina in CSF.
Roots are mobile and tend to move away from the needle, whereas the cord is fixed and vulnerable.
Neonatal cord ends lower, about L3.
Differential growth of the column compared with the cord explains the ascent.
questions.explanation: Because the cord ends higher than the sac, a lumbar cistern puncture reaches CSF without the cord. In infants the cord has not yet ascended as far, so a lower interspace is needed.

questions.stem: Describe the surface landmarks used to locate the L3-L4 interspace and explain why positioning the patient is important.
markingGuide: Highest points of the iliac crests joined by the supracristal plane.
Plane crosses at L4 or L4-L5.
Palpate spinous processes in the midline.
Flexed position opens the interspinous and interlaminar spaces.
questions.explanation: The crest line is an easily felt landmark that corresponds to L4. Positioning improves access by widening the gaps between the bones.
